setting.note: A Trojan refugee carries the survivors of a burning city west across the Mediterranean, is nearly held in Carthage by love, and fights his way into Latium to found the line that will become Rome; the poem's destination is the real hill Rome grew on, though its founding is legend.

rights.originalWork: Latin epic by Virgil, composed between about 29 and 19 BCE and long out of copyright. Mapped as a cited work: no text stored, no passages reproduced. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of any text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: The Aeneid, Virgil. Locations mapped by Read the Places; legendary sitings are noted as such.

palette.note: The fire of Troy the poem opens in and the blood of the Latin war it ends in. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; it still has to be legible, and this clears WCAG AA on paper.
